summary: Deep internet survey of ALL NES-on-FPGA implementations: mapper handling, ROM loading, video/palette, resource fit — synthesized into a recommendation for BulbuLator (Zynq-7010, PCAP core-reload)

result.landscape:
THE OPEN NES-ON-FPGA LANDSCAPE (ranked by relevance to a small Zynq-7010 with ARM control plane + PCAP core-reload):

ONE FAMILY DOMINATES. Every practical open core descends from Ludvig "Ludde" Strigeus' fpganes (GPL-2.0, originally Xilinx ISE on Nexys4/Artix-7). The lineage is: fpganes -> MiSTer-devel/NES_MiSTer (Kitrinx et al.; the full cart.sv all-mapper dispatcher, ~150 mappers, save-states) -> ports: NESTang (nand2mario, Gowin GW2AR-18), openFPGA-NES (agg23 / spiritualized1997, Analogue Pocket), nes_ecp5 (ULX3S/ECP5, Yosys), NES260 (KV260/ZU5EV). A parallel light-framework port is mist-devel/nes (Till Harbaum), same fpganes DNA but wrapped in a thin RGB+SD-MCU shell rather than the Cyclone-V-only MiSTer sys/. Brian Bennett's fpga_nes (BSD-2) is a separate, clean, well-commented but NROM-ONLY implementation — a great reference/validation oracle, architecturally a dead end for mappers (PRG/CHR in fixed BRAM, no banking).

RANKED RELEVANCE FOR BULBULATOR:
1. NESTang RTL (src/cart.sv + game_loader.v, the verbatim Kitrinx code). MOST relevant: it PROVES the exact all-mapper MiSTer cart + full ~150-mapper set synthesizes and runs on a SMALL non-Altera FPGA (Gowin GW2AR-18 = 20,736 LUT4 / 15,552 FF) alongside HDMI + SDRAM controller + a RISC-V loader softcore. Strip the RISC-V (the ARM replaces it) and HDMI (BulbuLator already has it) and the NES fabric alone is well under half a 7010. This is the closest existing analogue to your architecture.
2. MiSTer-devel/NES_MiSTer. The canonical, best-maintained, widest-coverage source. Vendor its rtl/cart.sv, rtl/mappers/*, ppu.sv, apu.sv; discard the Altera sys/ framework (HPS_IO, ascal scaler, DDR arbiter, save-state regs) and substitute BulbuLator's ARM + AXI + DDR-framebuffer chain.
3. mist-devel/nes. Useful as a REFERENCE for a thin wrapper: shows how the same core is fed by a light SD-MCU + RGB shell instead of MiSTer sys/. Mapper coverage is back-ported to near-MiSTer parity.
4. openFPGA-NES (agg23/spiritualized1997). MOST relevant as the reference implementation of the PER-MAPPER-GROUP + full-fabric-reload strategy (Chip32 loader parses header, reloads one of 4 bitstreams: NTSC_SET1/SET2, PAL_SET1/SET2). This is precisely BulbuLator's PCAP-reload pattern; study it if the all-in-one route hits a timing wall.
5. Brian Bennett fpga_nes (BSD-2). Reference/oracle only. Its NesDbg on-target 6502/PPU unit tests and clean rp2a03.v are gold for bringing up and cross-checking the CPU/PPU; do not build mappers on it.
6. danstrother's Spartan-3 core. Not a build target, but the ONLY public clean per-module resource breakdown that exists — the numbers that anchor the whole fit argument (see resourceFit).
7. NES260 (ZU5EV). A true "NES on Zynq" but exploits 2,304 KB on-chip UltraRAM that a 7010 does NOT have. Proof-of-concept only; its memory architecture is a trap on 7-series — follow MiSTer's DDR model instead.

Kevtris' Analogue Nt / Nt Mini core (279 mappers, authored the NES2.0 spec) is CLOSED/PROPRIETARY — reference for behavior/mapper-count expectations only, never for code.

UNVERIFIED: "lukeb00" and "hydra" could not be confirmed as real nodes in this lineage from public sources; treat as noise.
result.mapperStrategyComparison:
THREE STRATEGIES, MEASURED AGAINST BULBULATOR (owner's model: read mapper from .nes -> bring up core with that mapper -> load ROM, via dynamic-enable OR multiple cores):

(A) ALL-IN-ONE / DYNAMIC MAPPER ENABLE (one bitstream, every mapper compiled in, runtime one-hot select).
HOW: cart.sv (cart_top) instantiates every mapper module in parallel; a 1024-bit one-hot `wire [1023:0] me; me[{flags[18:17],flags[7:0]}]=1'b1;` lights exactly one; each mapper's `.enable` is an OR of the me[] bits it serves; outputs resolve on tri0/tri1 wired-OR buses ({prg_aout,chr_aout,prg_dout,vram_a10,vram_ce,irq,audio,...}) that the synthesizer folds into a mux ("not more than one mapper active at a time, so no conflicts").
PROS: This IS owner's "dynamic mapper enable" option. Switching GAMES is a register write — ZERO reload, instant, RetroPie-feel. It is the UNIVERSAL community pattern (MiSTer, NESTang, openFPGA, Kevtris all do variants of it); nobody maintains per-mapper logic separately. Mappers are cheap (~1-1.5k LUT4 total per danstrother; "more than the rest of the NES combined" but still ~1k LUT6-equiv). Simplest to operate.
CONS: On a DENSE 7010 the monolithic tri-state wired-OR at full mapper count is the one block that stresses ROUTING/fmax (not area). The Analogue Pocket — Cyclone V ~49k LE, LARGER than a 7010 — could NOT fit MiSTer's complete set in one image (it dropped VRC7 audio and split SET1/SET2), which is the cautionary data point. Counter-evidence: NESTang fits the FULL ~150-mapper set in a 20,736-LUT4 Gowin with a RISC-V and HDMI on top, so the Pocket split was largely framework+save-state+scaler pressure, not the bare mapper mux.

(B) PER-MAPPER(-GROUP) BITSTREAM + FULL-FABRIC RELOAD (owner's "multiple cores" option).
HOW: Group mappers by silicon family into 2-4 bitstreams; ARM reads the header, picks the matching .bit.bin, PCAP-reloads, then streams PRG/CHR. This is EXACTLY the Analogue Pocket Chip32 loader (4 bitstreams) and EXACTLY BulbuLator's proven v0.15.144 pl_reload()+fabric_reinit path.
PROS: Each image is small/lean and easy to close timing on a tight 7010; sidesteps the monolithic-cart routing risk. Reuses infrastructure you already shipped end-to-end on hardware. Suggested grouping mirrors Pocket SET1/SET2: GROUP-A discrete/generic+NROM+MMC1 (~50%+ of library), GROUP-B MMC3-family+MMC5+Namco118 (~25%), GROUP-C expansion-audio VRC/Namco163/Sunsoft/FDS, GROUP-D pirate/multicart (15/225/226/227/255 — the Dendy famiclone carts).
CONS: A sub-second PCAP reload on every ROM load whose mapper isn't in the resident image (owner has already accepted this latency for MACHINE switches). More build/verification surface (N bitstreams to regression-test).

(C) TRUE DYNAMIC PARTIAL RECONFIGURATION (reprogram only a mapper pblock while the core runs).
VERDICT: UNUSED anywhere in the retro-FPGA community. No NES project does Xilinx/Intel PR for mappers. It is pure floorplanning overhead for logic that is cheaper to always include. DO NOT pursue. The community "equivalent" of PR is full-fabric reload — which for BulbuLator is PCAP, i.e. strategy (B).

WHAT THE COMMUNITY ACTUALLY USES: (A) on large FPGAs; (B) on small FPGAs (the Pocket). (C) never.

BEST FIT FOR BULBULATOR: a TIERED hybrid that leans on (A) but keeps (B) as the escape hatch — see recommendedMapperStrategy. Both tiers are literally the two options the owner pre-approved, and both reuse assets already on the board.
result.recommendedCore:
BASE ON THE MiSTer NES_MiSTer RTL, taken via the NESTang variant as the porting template.

WHY THIS CORE:
- MAPPER COVERAGE: ~150 mappers in one dispatcher (cart.sv + rtl/mappers/{MMC1,MMC2,MMC3,MMC5,VRC,Namco,Sunsoft,JYCompany,Sachen,FDS,Mapper99,generic,misc}.sv), covering 0-255 plus 268/413/547, i.e. essentially the entire playable NES/Famicom/Dendy library including expansion-audio and pirate/multicart boards. This is the "ALL cartridge types" the owner asked for.
- PROVEN SMALL-FPGA FIT: NESTang runs this exact Kitrinx cart.sv + full mapper set on a Gowin GW2AR-18 (20,736 LUT4) with a RISC-V loader and HDMI on top. Strip both (ARM replaces the softcore; you already have HDMI) and the NES+mappers block is ~4-6k LUT6 and <10 BRAM — coexists comfortably with your DDR/HDMI/control-plane inside 17.6k LUT6.
- CLEAN INTERFACE BOUNDARIES: The core is decoupled at exactly the three seams you need to re-host. (1) VIDEO: ppu.sv emits a 6-bit palette index `wire [5:0] color` -> a small runtime-loadable palette LUT -> RGB; trivially re-pointed at your fb chain. (2) INPUT: a byte controller port; NES's 8 buttons map 1:1 to your 8-bit JOY_STATE. (3) ROM/MEMORY: a GameLoader + a documented flat memory map (PRG@0, CHR@2 MiB/bit21, CARTRAM/save@16 MiB/bit24) that already assumes external DRAM — you point it at PS DDR over AXI-HP instead of SDRAM.
- ARM-LOADS-THE-CORE MODEL: MiSTer's "HPS parses the file and streams it to the fabric" is identical to what BulbuLator already does for ZX snapshots/tapes and to your v0.15.144 core-reload flow.

WHY NOT the alternatives: Brian Bennett fpga_nes is BSD (nice) but NROM-only with PRG/CHR baked into BRAM and no banking — a rewrite to add mappers, so use it only as a bring-up/validation oracle (its NesDbg on-target 6502/PPU unit tests are genuinely valuable). mist-devel/nes is the same core in a lighter shell — mine it for wrapper ideas but the RTL is the same MiSTer lineage. NES260's UltraRAM approach doesn't port to 7-series.

LICENSE: NES_MiSTer / NESTang are GPL-3.0 (fpganes ancestor is GPL-2.0). BulbuLator is GPL-2.0-OR-LATER, and "or-later" is forward-compatible with GPL-3.0, so combining is clean — the resulting NES core is effectively GPL-3.0. Add Strigeus + MiSTer/Kitrinx/Sorgelig + NESTang to THIRD_PARTY.md/NOTICE and pin upstream by SHA in get_deps.sh (matches your self-contained-steps discipline). Keep git history clean (no co-author/generated-by trailers per your global rules).

ONE LICENSE CAVEAT TO CHECK BEFORE SHIPPING: the CPU. MiSTer swapped in T65 (Daniel Wallner's VHDL 6502), which historically shipped with a non-standard/ambiguous "free/non-commercial-flavored" header rather than a clean OSI license. Read the actual rtl/t65/*.vhd headers. If ambiguous, swap for a cleanly-licensed 6502 (Arlet Ottens', or a BSD 6502, or Strigeus' original custom 2A03) — the T65 presents a standard 6502 bus so the swap is low-risk. Do this before redistribution, not before first bring-up.
result.recommendedMapperStrategy:
TIERED HYBRID: "curated all-in-one first, PCAP per-mapper-group as the escape hatch." This deliberately realises BOTH owner-approved options and picks between them by empirical synthesis result rather than guesswork.

TIER 1 (ship this first — dynamic mapper enable, option A): ONE NES bitstream containing the common mapper set that covers ~95% of the library: NROM(0), MMC1(1), UxROM(2), CNROM(3), MMC3(4), AxROM(7), plus generic.sv's Mapper28 meta-mapper (folds 0/2/3/7 and other discrete carts into one configurable block to save LUTs) and MMC5(5). Coverage is extremely front-loaded: MMC1~28% + MMC3~24% + UxROM~11% + NROM~10% + CNROM~6% + AxROM~3% ≈ 83% from six mappers; the curated set clears ~95%. In this tier, changing GAMES is a pure register write — no reload, instant. This fits the 7010 with large margin and closes timing easily.

TIER 2 (breadth — decided by synthesis): ADD the rest (VRC1-7, Namco163, Sunsoft-5B/FME-7, FDS, JYCompany, Sachen, the pirate/multicart group 15/225/226/227/255 that Dendy famiclones need). Then run synthesis + timing at the NES master clock on the actual 7010:
- IF the full monolithic cart closes timing and fits (NESTang evidence says it likely will once RISC-V/HDMI are stripped) -> KEEP the single all-in-one bitstream. Best UX: every cartridge, zero reload.
- IF the tri-state wired-OR at full mapper count blows routing/fmax on the dense 7010 (the Analogue Pocket cautionary case) -> FALL BACK to option B: split into 2-4 mapper-GROUP bitstreams by silicon family (GROUP-A discrete+NROM+MMC1; GROUP-B MMC3-family+MMC5; GROUP-C expansion-audio VRC/N163/Sunsoft/FDS; GROUP-D pirate/multicart), and have the ARM PCAP-reload the matching group AFTER parsing the header. This is exactly the Analogue Pocket Chip32 pattern and exactly your proven v0.15.144 pl_reload()/fabric_reinit path.

WHY THIS IS RIGHT: (1) It never promises a UX you can't deliver — Tier 1 works on day one regardless of how synthesis lands. (2) It maps 1:1 onto owner's stated architecture ("dynamic enable OR multiple cores"). (3) The fallback reuses infrastructure already validated on hardware, so the risk of the "hard" path is low. (4) NEVER reduce functionality (per your standing rule): the group-split path preserves 100% mapper coverage — it trades a sub-second reload on exotic ROMs (which the owner has already accepted for machine switches) for timing closure, rather than dropping mappers. Only drop mappers (e.g. VRC7 FM audio, as the Pocket did) as an absolute last resort if BOTH all-in-one and grouping fail.

DO NOT use partial reconfiguration — unused by the entire community, pure overhead. Your per-fabric PCAP swap is the correct and only reconfig granularity.
result.romLoadingSpec:
EXACT iNES/NES2.0 LOAD PATH THE ARM MUST IMPLEMENT (the ARM plays MiSTer's "HPS"; this mirrors your existing ZX SD->DDR + AXI-config plumbing).

FILE LAYOUT ON SD (FAT32): [16-byte header][optional 512-byte trainer][PRG-ROM][CHR-ROM].

HEADER PARSE (16 bytes, byte indices per nesdev):
- byte0-3: magic must be 4E 45 53 1A ("NES"+EOF). Reject otherwise.
- byte4: PRG-ROM size in 16 KiB units (iNES). 
- byte5: CHR-ROM size in 8 KiB units; byte5==0 => board uses CHR-RAM (has_chr_ram=1), default 8 KiB.
- byte6 (flags6): bit0 mirroring (0=vertical/1=horizontal), bit1 battery-backed PRG-RAM present, bit2 512-byte trainer present, bit3 four-screen, bits7-4 = mapper LOW nibble.
- byte7 (flags7): bits1-0 console type, bits3-2 => NES2.0 if ==2'b10 (i.e. (byte7 & 0x0C)==0x08), bits7-4 = mapper HIGH nibble.
- mapper = {byte7[7:4], byte6[7:4]} (8-bit). NES2.0 extends: mapper bits11-8 = byte8[3:0] (12-bit, 0-4095) and submapper = byte8[7:4].
- NES2.0 sizing: exponent form when the size MSB nibble is 0xF, else (MSB_nibble<<8 | LSB) units. PRG/CHR-RAM sizes from byte10/11 shift counts (size = 64 << n). NVRAM/battery size from byte10 upper nibble.
- REGION (critical for Dendy): NES2.0 byte12[1:0] = 0 NTSC / 1 PAL / 2 multi / 3 Dendy. iNES1.0 has only byte9 bit0 TV system.
- DIRTY-HEADER GUARD (replicate MiSTer's is_dirty): if NOT NES2.0 and bytes 9-15 contain non-zero garbage, ZERO the mapper high nibble (byte7[7:4]) — many old dumps have junk there.

ARM ACTIONS:
1. Read+validate header; skip 512 bytes if trainer bit (byte6 bit2) set.
2. Compute mapper, submapper, prg_bytes, chr_bytes, has_chr_ram, mirroring, four_screen, battery, region. Compute prg_mask/chr_mask as the power-of-two masks the fabric ANDs bank bits with.
3. (Tier-2/group path only) pick the matching .bit.bin from 0:/CORES/, PCAP-reload, run fabric_reinit_after_reload().
4. DMA PRG then CHR into PS DDR at the fixed base offsets from cart.sv's map: PRG @ DDR base 0x000000, CHR @ bit21 (2 MiB), CART/save RAM @ bit24 (16 MiB); CPU-RAM/CHR-VRAM at their fixed high prefixes. For CHR-RAM (byte5==0) write nothing — just make the $0000-$1FFF region writable (chr_allow) so the PPU fills it.
5. Write the 64-bit mapper_flags word over AXI (your MACHINE_CFG-style register). REUSE MiSTer's exact bit contract so the vendored fabric decodes it unchanged: [7:0]=mapper, [10:8]=prg_size class, [13:11]=chr_size class, [14]=mirroring, [15]=has_chr_ram, [16]=four_screen, [24:17]=NES2.0 high mapper/submapper, [25]=battery, [29:26]=prgram, [34:31]=prg_nvram, [35]=is_nes20, [37:36]=timing/region, [44:43]=console type, [48:45]=Vs PPU, [52:49]=Vs hardware.
6. Release reset; the in-fabric mapper now translates CPU $8000-$FFFF -> linear PRG addr and PPU $0000-$1FFF -> linear CHR addr against DDR over AXI-HP. AXI-HP IS the emulated cartridge bus.

BATTERY/SAVE (.sav): PRG-RAM at CPU $6000-$7FFF, usually 8 KiB, in a small dual-port BRAM. If battery bit set, ARM restores 0:/NES/<name>.sav on load and persists it back on eject/menu-exit (MiSTer's bram/bk_save behaviour). 8 KiB is trivial BRAM.

FDS: needs a BIOS (disksys.rom / boot0.rom) the ARM must also stage into DDR.

MEMORY DISCIPLINE (non-negotiable on 7010): PRG (up to ~1 MiB on MMC5), CHR-ROM/RAM, and WRAM live in PS DDR over AXI-HP — NEVER BRAM. 60 BRAM36 = ~262 KB total can't hold a big cart plus a framebuffer. BRAM holds only the small internal state: 2 KiB CPU RAM, 2 KiB nametable VRAM, 256 B OAM, 32 B palette, 8 KiB save SRAM, and the palette LUT. NES clocks are slow (master ~21.48 MHz, CPU ~1.79 MHz) so DDR latency is a non-issue — but reuse your ZX AXI-HP latency-gate/harness so a slow DDR read never corrupts a cartridge fetch.
result.videoPaletteSpec:
NES PALETTE -> RGB888, FED THROUGH BULBULATOR'S SRC_BPP-PARAMETERISED fb_line_disp.

THE KEY LEVERAGE: your fb_line_disp already does palette-index -> RGB888 at fixed 1280x720 and is SRC_BPP-parameterised. The 2C02 PPU emits exactly a palette INDEX per pixel — it has NO native RGB (it outputs composite NTSC; every core bakes its own decoded LUT). So the NES maps onto your existing chain almost perfectly: widen the framebuffer capture bpp and load a NES palette into the palette RAM.

INDEX WIDTH:
- Base: PPU color is 6-bit (0-63, $00-$3F). Of 64 codes only ~52-55 are visually distinct (several blacks collapse; $0F is canonical black).
- Emphasis: PPUMASK bits 5/6/7 (red/green/blue tint) attenuate the signal, giving an effective 9-bit selector (512 entries) if honored.
RECOMMENDATION: set SRC_BPP=8 and capture an 8-bit index = {2'b0, color[5:0]} for a first pass (64-entry palette, emphasis ignored — most content looks right). For full emphasis accuracy, set SRC_BPP=9 (or pre-combine emphasis into the index in the video module) and load a 512-entry palette. Do NOT expose the raw index to any downstream mixer — index->RGB happens in the palette stage you already own.

PALETTE CONTENT: bake a good composite-DECODED RGB888 table (do not attempt real-time NTSC decode in fabric — nobody does; precompute offline). Use a well-regarded pack: FirebrandX, FCEUX, Nestopia, or nes_ntsc/Bisqwit-generated. .pal files are 192 bytes (64 x RGB) or 1536 bytes (512 x RGB for emphasis). Make it ARM-LOADABLE into palette RAM (exactly MiSTer/openFPGA .pal behaviour) so the notoriously subjective NES colors are swappable without resynthesis — same pattern as your ZX palette RAM. Widen the palette RAM entries to RGB888 (24-bit) to match fb_line_disp's output.

WIRING INTO THE FB CHAIN:
- PPU renders native 256x240 @ ~60 Hz (NTSC/Dendy) / 50 Hz (PAL). ppu.sv gives `color[5:0]` + a ~5.37 MHz dot clock-enable (ce_pix) + HBlank/VBlank/HSync/VSync.
- Write the native 256x240 indexed frame into your DDR framebuffer (reuse the ZX tear-free triple-buffer path); tag SRC_BPP=8 (or 9). fb_line_disp reads it, does palette->RGB888, outputs at 1280x720.
- SCALING: 5x horizontal (5*256 = 1280) and 3x vertical (3*240 = 720) hits 1280x720 EXACTLY with clean integer scaling — no fractional resampler needed, reuse the ZX scaler with per-core ratios. Note NES pixel aspect is 8:7 (so 5:3 pixel scaling is close to correct 4:3-ish; acceptable, tune per taste). If you overscan to 256x224, adjust vertical scale/centering.

REGION / DENDY (owner wants Dendy): ship SEPARATE palette LUTs per region and gate CPU:PPU timing on a region config bit. NTSC 2C02: CPU:PPU 1:3, 20 vblank scanlines, master ~21.48 MHz. Dendy (Russian famiclone): NTSC-like 2A03/2C02 behaviour but 50 Hz with 51 extra idle scanlines — distinct from true PAL. True PAL 2C07: -15° hue shift ($x7 vs $x8 colorburst), red/green emphasis bits SWAPPED vs 2C02, CPU:PPU 1:3.2, 70 vblank scanlines, master 26.6017125 MHz. The region bit comes straight from mapper_flags[37:36] which the ARM set from NES2.0 byte12. For Dendy famiclone multicarts, also ensure the pirate/multicart mapper group is present (see mapper strategy).

integrationPlan.detail: Add MiSTer-devel/NES_MiSTer (or NESTang's proven-portable copy) rtl/{cart.sv, ppu.sv, apu.sv, nes.v, mappers/*} + T65 to the repo via get_deps.sh pinned by SHA. Add THIRD_PARTY.md/NOTICE entries (Strigeus, Kitrinx/Sorgelig, nand2mario). Do NOT bring the Altera sys/ (HPS_IO, ascal, DDR arbiter, save-state regs, cheat engine).

Read rtl/t65/*.vhd headers. If ambiguous/non-OSI, swap T65 for a clean-licensed 6502 (Arlet Ottens' or a BSD 2A03). Standard 6502 bus => low-risk swap. Bring-up can start on T65; resolve before redistribution.

integrationPlan.step: 3. Retarget cartridge memory to PS DDR
integrationPlan.detail: Replace sdram.sv/MemoryController with your AXI-HP DDR path. Honor cart.sv's map: PRG@0, CHR@bit21(2MiB), CART/save@bit24(16MiB). Reuse the ZX AXI-HP latency-gate/harness. Keep only CPU-RAM(2K)/VRAM(2K)/OAM/palette/save-SRAM(8K) in BRAM.

Expose the 64-bit mapper_flags as a MACHINE_CFG-style AXI register with MiSTer's exact bit layout ([7:0]=mapper, [10:8]/[13:11]=sizes, [14]=mirror, [15]=chr_ram, [24:17]=high mapper/submapper, [25]=battery, [35]=nes20, [37:36]=region). Fabric decodes it unchanged.

Port GameLoader logic to C on ARM: validate 4E45531A, skip 512B trainer, compute mapper/submapper/sizes/mirroring/battery/region + is_dirty guard, DMA PRG then CHR into DDR at the fixed offsets, write mapper_flags, release reset. Reuse the ZX SD/FAT + AXI download plumbing.

integrationPlan.step: 6. Graft video into the fb chain
integrationPlan.detail: Tap ppu.sv color[5:0] + ce_pix + blanks. Set SRC_BPP=8 (index={2'b0,color}); load a 64-entry RGB888 NES palette (FirebrandX/FCEUX .pal) into ARM-writable palette RAM. Write 256x240 indexed frames to the DDR triple-buffer; scale 5x/3x to exact 1280x720. Ship per-region palettes. (Later: SRC_BPP=9 + 512-entry for emphasis.)
Map the 8 NES buttons (A,B,Select,Start,Up,Down,Left,Right) 1:1 onto the existing 8-bit JOY_STATE from the PS2->joystick path. Add MACHINE_ID so the control plane recognizes the NES core.

Synthesize the curated common-mapper set (0/1/2/3/4/7 + generic Mapper28 + MMC5). Read utilisation/timing. Validate NROM (SMB, Excitebike), MMC1, MMC3, UxROM, CNROM, AxROM on hardware. Use Brian Bennett's NesDbg unit-test expectations as a CPU/PPU oracle.
ARM restores/persists 0:/NES/<name>.sav for battery carts on load/eject. Stage FDS BIOS (disksys.rom) into DDR for FDS titles.

Add VRC/Namco163/Sunsoft/FDS/JYCompany/Sachen + pirate-multicart group (15/225/226/227/255 for Dendy). Synthesize the full monolithic cart on 7010. IF timing/area close (NESTang precedent) -> keep single all-in-one bitstream. IF the tri-state cart blows fmax/routing -> split into 2-4 mapper-GROUP .bit.bin and have ARM PCAP-reload the matching group after header parse (reuse v0.15.144 pl_reload/fabric_reinit).
Wire the .nes browser into the DN-style OSD; on select, ARM parses header, (group path) reloads the right core, streams ROM, resumes. Log to BUILD_HISTORY.md; update Obsidian vault + memory.

Gate CPU:PPU timing + palette on the region bit (NTSC/Dendy/PAL). Route APU (incl. DMC DMA) and expansion audio (VRC6/7, MMC5, N163, Sunsoft-5B on the shared `audio` bus) into BulbuLator's audio engine. Defer the VHDL save-state subsystem (heavy) unless requested.

risks: Timing/fmax of the monolithic cart.sv on a DENSE 7010: the 1024-wide one-hot + tri-state wired-OR at full mapper count is the single block most likely to fail routing/fmax (the Analogue Pocket — a LARGER Cyclone V — had to split it). Mitigation: Tier-1 curated set always closes; Tier-2 falls back to PCAP mapper-group bitstreams. Only NESTang evidence suggests the full set may still fit — must be confirmed by actual synthesis, not assumed.

No published exact LUT/BRAM/fmax numbers for NES_MiSTer on 7-series; all fit claims are extrapolations from danstrother (Spartan-3, ~5k LUT4) and NESTang (Gowin, ~20k LUT4). Synthesize EARLY (step 8) and read utilisation before committing to all-in-one.

DDR latency/bandwidth for the emulated cartridge bus: benign at NES clocks (CPU 1.79 MHz) but a mis-tuned AXI-HP path or missing latency-gate can corrupt PRG/CHR fetches. Reuse the ZX AXI-HP harness; do not hand-roll.
T65 CPU license ambiguity (non-OSI header) — must be resolved before redistribution of a GPL project; budget a 6502-swap task.
Combined work becomes effectively GPL-3.0 (NES_MiSTer/NESTang are GPLv3, fpganes GPLv2-only). Fine under BulbuLator's GPL-2.0-or-later, but note it pins the NES core to v3; update THIRD_PARTY/NOTICE.

Dendy support is real extra work: separate region timing (50 Hz, +51 idle scanlines, NTSC-like PPU) AND the pirate/multicart mapper group (15/225/226/227/255) that famiclone carts use — don't assume 'NTSC core' covers Dendy.

Expansion-audio mappers (VRC6/VRC7 FM, MMC5, N163, Sunsoft-5B, FDS) add the most logic and DSP; they're the first cut candidates if area is tight (the Pocket dropped VRC7 FM). Treat dropping any as a last resort per the never-reduce-functionality rule.
Save-state subsystem (savestates.vhd/statemanager.vhd, VHDL, DRAM-backed) is heavy — defer it for the first port; don't let it inflate the initial bitstream.

NES pixel aspect (8:7) vs the clean 5x/3x integer scale to 1280x720 is a minor geometry compromise; acceptable but confirm with the owner. Overscan (256x224 vs 240) also needs a per-core scaler setting.
NES260 (ZU5EV UltraRAM) and the Pocket's on-chip-RAM approaches are memory-architecture traps on 7010 — do NOT copy; PRG/CHR must go to PS DDR.
